findings.title: Mutable authority revisions invalidate a successful request's replay identity
findings.reproducer: Use the existing register fixture to commit descriptor id R and command C for actor character X/life L. In a later legitimate transaction retain X/L and the same locator container but advance recordUpdatedAt by 1, or update life revision/locationRevision/locator.revision after an ordinary move. Supply a current valid TrustedPoint whose verifier succeeds. Retry exact C and R within the once window. receiptFingerprint differs; once.ts:136 throws client_id_conflict before old receipt can return. No home/consent eligibility change is needed.
findings.impact: A successful old operation appears conflicting after ordinary settlement/travel, contradicting retained-success replay before current eligibility. Tests hold NOW and authority rows constant and miss it.
findings.repair: Separate stable request/participant identity from mutable commit read-set facts. Keep current-source verification for new mutations; do not recompute old receipt identity from current mutable revisions. Bind normalized command and immutable actor character/life, and enforce ownership of that exact life before exposing minimal receipt. If initial revision provenance must be retained, keep it in receipt-bound data and use that recorded provenance for old replay, not newly sampled values. Preserve kind/body conflicts and forbid rebinding to a new life.
findings.requiredEvidence: On real Node and Worker stores, commit then advance same-life authority timestamps/revisions/location and retry unchanged id/body before loader; expect original duplicate and no household writes/events. Different body or actor/life must refuse. Include inactive/archived ownership policy explicitly rather than falling back to current life.

findings.title: Missing own root still reads an inherited households getter
findings.reproducer: let hits=0; const db=Object.create({get households(){hits++; return createHouseholdCollection()}}); householdPoint(db,'households','00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002'). The descriptor is absent but rootOf line91 performs db.households, invoking the getter and accepting its root. A direct apply against a root supplied this way follows the same read at line84.
findings.impact: Violates the advertised no-getter and missing-vs-present boundary for malformed ordinary DB objects. Genuine Store proxies are not implicated; this is not a demonstrated remote exploit.
findings.repair: When no own root descriptor exists, return absent/create a new root without evaluating db.households. With an own data descriptor, retain the fixed-path get needed for the genuine Store proxy placeholder; keep accessor/nonenumerable/own-undefined refusals. Add inherited-root getter test along with ordinary/keyed present-row cases.
findings.requiredEvidence: Missing own root must produce absence without getter invocation; existing Node Store root placeholder and KeyedMap point rows must remain usable; raw own undefined stays invalid.

acceptedSourceProperties: f281 KeyedMap entry descriptor defect is fixed by isKeyedMap WeakMap brand at durableStorage:105. Genuine map get performs a point lookup; descriptor is only a presence marker. Ordinary row values come directly from descriptors and reject accessors/own undefined.
Fixed root access now supports Node Store's own descriptor placeholder. All eleven maps are registered in KEYED_SPECS. No household map enumeration is introduced by the entry lookup.

Adapter read fingerprints track exact loaded reducer rows/absence plus revision. Linked accepted invitation support reads join this set. Trusted source verifiers are accumulated and checked before application, including actor proof.

Apply checks all declared expectations and validates every write before applying any, rejects duplicate/unexpected writes, and caps expectations/writes/events. Its Result input is trusted reducer output, not a raw external patch parser.

Reducer changes versus 619 are domain event type-to-kind rename only, paired in records. consentView/lifeIdentity are unchanged. The event discriminant change avoids widening the WebSocket wire allowlist.

Once+patch share one Store transaction. Domain refusal throws out of transaction and formats outside; unknown read/write failures propagate. Service awaits transaction durability before returning events and returns events=[] for duplicate.

Node Store serializes callbacks and awaits file durability by default at store.ts:478-500. Worker stages session receipts and entries in the same transactionSync at sqlite-store.ts:645 onward, then waits barrier at 738-742.
Liabilities abort in service and apply. There is no no-op settlement or invented money authority.
importantLimits: Authority homes/lifeFacts/pairFacts are supplied externally but reducer expectations are checked against household mirror maps by durableApply:14-33. Future canonical readers/writers must maintain exact matching projected rows in this same transaction or intentionally revise that mapping; a verified external fact alone cannot satisfy the current apply layer. A missing mirror correctly causes refusal, not inferred authority.

TrustedPoint.verifyReadSet is a host contract. Current code cannot prove a dishonest/constant-true verifier checks session/device/account ownership, exact locator/container, home incarnation/scene revision and both pair sources. Existing tests use synthetic projections and do not establish canonical source authority.

Session authentication and system authority remain unimplemented. Service always requires a resolved session and present sessionLife before system loading. It is not directly callable from an already-open lifecycle transaction without deadlock risk from nesting store.transact. Do not fake a session or active life for system cleanup.

Every endMember produces a liability handoff even if money has never been used, so leave/revoke/terminate and close with active members fail closed. Accept must not be activated without a safe termination path; no residence grant follows from stored membership.

Events are only returned after commit; there is no durable outbox/dispatcher. A crash after commit before delivery followed by duplicate produces no event. This is not exactly-once or guaranteed eventual notification. Canonical state reads may recover UI; financial/lifecycle obligations cannot rely on this event channel.

ctx.once may initialize/prune expired receipts on successful replay. No household/event mutation does not imply zero entire-store writes. It retains only its configured live window and performs inherited bounded-player/global Node recount work; Worker uses SQL counts.

Collection root Reflect.ownKeys and malformed object ownKeys allocate whole key lists before length rejection. Valid schema/loader reads are bounded; arbitrary corrupt-object CPU is not strictly capped. Locator/byCharacterLife maps have no validateStoredRow validator and no production writer, so they remain unusable authority slots.

Five tests cover synthetic register only. Node uses actual file Store entries mode. Worker-labelled tests use createSqliteStore over node:sqlite testStorage, not actual workerd/DO HTTP. No durable invite/accept/close matrix, canonical lifecycle, event delivery, liability consumer or host endpoint proof.

No local runtime, compiler, tests or build executed. Exact-candidate compiler/Node/actual Worker durability and failure evidence remains required. Worker barrier failure is uncertain durability, not proof that commit rolled back.
